Test differences between networks by permutation

Source: R/permutation_htna.R
permutation_htna.Rd

permutation_htna() tests by permutation whether two heterogeneous transition networks, for example of two groups of learners or two phases of a study, differ more than chance would produce. The sessions behind both networks are pooled, the group labels are shuffled many times, both networks are re-estimated on every shuffle, and each observed difference is compared with the shuffled ones. Each edge gets a p-value and an effect size (the observed difference divided by the standard deviation of the shuffled differences), and the networks as a whole are tested with the sum and the maximum of the absolute differences. Because whole sessions are shuffled, the nesting of transitions in sessions is respected.

permutation_htna() runs Nestimate's permutation() with the actor partition kept. It tests two htna networks estimated with the same method on the same codes, or every pair of cohorts of a grouped network. With many edges some fall below alpha by chance; set adjust (for example "BH") to correct for multiple testing. With measures, node centralities are tested as well. It returns a net_permutation object, or one per cohort pair for a grouped network.

A small p-value says that a difference is larger than the shuffles produce, not how large or how probable it is, which bayes_compare_htna() estimates. compare_htna() gives descriptive differences per actor pair, and plot_htna_diff() draws the result.

Usage

permutation_htna(x, y = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x, y

Two htna networks, or an htna_group in x with y = NULL, in which case every pair of cohorts is tested.

...

Settings: iter (shuffles, default 1000), alpha (0.05), paired (FALSE), adjust (multiplicity correction, "none"), measures (centralities to test), nlambda, seed and actor (shuffle whole actors).

Value

For two networks, an object of class net_permutation; for a grouped network, a named list of class c("net_permutation_group", "list") with one result per cohort pair (for example "Early vs Late"). Both have print() and summary() methods; summary() returns a data frame with one row per edge (and pair) and columns from, to, weight_x, weight_y, diff, effect_size, p_value and sig. Differences are x - y.

See also

bayes_compare_htna(), compare_htna(), plot_htna_diff().

Examples

data(human_ai)
grp <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type", group = "phase")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'cluster' (24 sessions), 'actor_type' (9 sessions)
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (18 sessions), 'actor_type' (15 sessions)
perm <- permutation_htna(grp, iter = 50, seed = 1)
perm
#> Grouped Permutation Test
#> Groups: Early vs Late 
#> 
#> -- Early vs Late --
#> Permutation Test: Transition Network (relative probabilities) [directed]
#>   Iterations: 50  |  Alpha: 0.05
#>   Nodes: 12  |  Edges tested: 135  |  Significant: 25
#>   Global test (networks differ overall?): M = 2.760 (p = 0.0196)  |  S = 0.181 (p = 0.0196)
head(summary(perm))
#>           group from        to   weight_x   weight_y          diff effect_size
#> 1 Early vs Late  Ask       Ask 0.01827676 0.01819686  0.0000799055  0.01280436
#> 2 Early vs Late  Ask     Check 0.06875544 0.05789909  0.0108563494  1.12598665
#> 3 Early vs Late  Ask   Execute 0.03307224 0.01157982  0.0214924187  2.62829072
#> 4 Early vs Late  Ask Frustrate 0.09921671 0.13151365 -0.0322969375 -2.23575725
#> 5 Early vs Late  Ask   Inquire 0.05395997 0.07196030 -0.0180003326 -1.53373385
#> 6 Early vs Late  Ask      Plan 0.43342037 0.38544251  0.0479778511  1.59966614
#>      p_value   sig
#> 1 1.00000000 FALSE
#> 2 0.27450980 FALSE
#> 3 0.03921569  TRUE
#> 4 0.03921569  TRUE
#> 5 0.11764706 FALSE
#> 6 0.13725490 FALSE
